# App parity: which apps keep up with the framework

<!-- Generated by `scripts/check-app-parity.sh --write` from the apps and docs/app-parity.toml. Don't edit by hand. -->

When the framework gains a better way to do something, every app moves to it, or the lag is written down with the wave of the plan that catches it up. `scripts/check-app-parity.sh` (in `make validate` and Linux CI) fails on a lag that isn't listed in [app-parity.toml](app-parity.toml) and on a listed lag that has been fixed, so the list only shrinks. A framework change that replaces something apps do themselves adds a rule here and moves every app in the same PR, or lists the ones it didn't ([AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)). A rule proves adoption: the old way is gone. Where a test can show the framework helper is used correctly (logs actually arrive, a retry repeats the operation), the same PR adds that test too.

## Rules

| Rule | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `forgekit` | Uses the ForgeKit package |
| `forge-host` | Rust core on the forge-app runtime, hosted by ForgeHost |
| `appkit-alerts` | Errors shown with ForgeAppKit's `forgeAlert`, no own ErrorAlert.swift |
| `errors-shown` | A failed action says so: no `try?` on a change, no empty catch-all |
| `alerts-on-top` | App-wide alerts on the navigation stack or tabs, never on a first screen that pushes others |
| `alerts-over-sheets` | A model alert is held back while a sheet is up; the sheet shows alerts itself |
| `picked-files` | Picked files copied with ForgeAppKit's `ForgePickedFile` (off the main thread), never by hand |
| `web-images` | Pictures from the web through `ForgeRemoteImage` (kept on disk, decoded at the size shown), never `AsyncImage` |
| `state-views` | Empty, no-results, loading and failed screens through ForgeUI's `ForgeStateView` |
| `toned-text` | Warning and error text in ForgeUI's tones, never raw orange, yellow or (for errors) red |
| `feedback` | Outcome haptics (success, failure) through ForgeAppKit's `ForgeFeedback` |
| `forgeui-appearance` | Launch appearance from ForgeUI, no own LaunchAppearance.swift |
| `urlsession` | iOS requests through the URLSession `http` service |
| `location` | Location through the `location` service |
| `rust-cancellation` | Rust work cancelled from Swift through ForgeKit's `withRustCancellation` |
| `swift-logging` | Swift logs through `ForgeLog`, never `print` or `NSLog` |
| `connectivity` | Network changes through the `connectivity` service, no own `NWPathMonitor` |
| `requirements` | requirements.toml, every requirement with a test |
| `device-checks` | Every requirement has a device scenario |
| `ui-test` | At least one `uitests/*.toml` scenario for `forge ui run` |
| `device-lab` | Reachable from Device Lab's Apps screen |
| `device-family` | Says which devices it runs on (`[ios] devices`) |

A rule an app doesn't meet is one of: **No** (missing: the app should use the framework and doesn't yet, with the wave that fixes it), **Deferred** (known work postponed on purpose, with the wave) or **Not applicable** (the app has a real reason for its own plumbing). Whether an app has been proven on an iPhone is a separate question, answered in [device-validation.md](device-validation.md).

## Known lag

| App | Rule | Status | Why | Wave |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| checklist | `device-checks` | missing | CL-3 (background and cancelling) is proved by twin tests only; a phone scenario needs a slow search to interrupt | 4 |
| commonplace | `device-checks` | missing | CP-5 (error words) needs the fixture server offline, and CP-7 (Stop ends a refresh in Rust) a feed that hangs; written with slice 2 | 4 |
| good-dog | `device-checks` | missing | GD requirements without a scenario yet; written with GD2b's phone run | 4 |
| relay | `device-checks` | missing | CH-12 (Chat's, now Relay's messaging: data held by a second core) is proved by its twin test only; the phone can't open a second core from the UI | 4 |
| sketchbook | `requirements` | missing | Written as the Soundscape and Sketchbook features are finished | 4 |
| soundscape | `requirements` | missing | Written as the Soundscape and Sketchbook features are finished | 4 |

## Not applicable

| App | Rule | Why |
|---|---|---|
| device-lab | `forge-host` | LabModel's state is lab services (sensors, permissions, hosting the other apps), not an app core (decided 2026-11-15) |
